items.title: Jurassic Park
items.line: Opened in the US on 11 June 1993. Industrial Light & Magic's computer dinosaurs helped it take $914 million in its first run, the biggest film ever until Titanic.

items.title: Schindler's List
items.line: Spielberg shot it in black and white in Krakow from March 1993, while editing Jurassic Park in the evenings. It won seven Oscars, including Best Picture.

items.title: Doom
items.line: id Software put the first episode online at midnight on 10 December 1993 and let people copy it. By June 1996 it had reportedly been downloaded 20 million times.

items.title: The X-Files
items.line: Fox aired the pilot on 10 September 1993. Mulder and Scully drew about 12 million viewers, and season one averaged 11.21 million.

items.title: NCSA Mosaic
items.line: Version 1.0 of the browser appeared on 21 April 1993. It was the first to show images inline with text, and its creators went on to found Netscape.

items.title: Mortal Kombat
items.line: The home versions landed on 13 September 1993, 'Mortal Monday'. On the Genesis a cheat code unlocked the blood, while the SNES version swapped it for sweat.
